title: Prospective study comparing conventional coagulation diagnostics with viscoelastometry in patients requiring reversal of the effects of oral anticoagulants
summary:
This study investigates how reliably new, so-called viscoelastic methods (e.g. ROTEM or ClotPro) can measure blood coagulability compared to conventional laboratory tests when the effect of oral anticoagulants needs to be reversed in patients.

Oral anticoagulants (e.g. certain blood thinners) are often used to prevent thrombosis or stroke. However, if emergency treatment or surgery becomes necessary, their effect must be reversed quickly and safely to prevent bleeding. A reliable assessment of blood coagulation is crucial for this.

In this prospective observational study, blood samples are therefore taken from affected patients in order to compare different coagulation tests. In addition to routine coagulation diagnostics, special laboratory tests for thrombin generation (e.g. thrombin-antithrombin complexes and thrombinoscopy) are also carried out in a reference laboratory.

The aim is to test whether point-of-care viscoelastometry (rapid coagulation tests performed directly at the patient's bedside) is a reliable alternative to established laboratory procedures and can therefore enable faster and more precise treatment decisions in the future.

interventions.name:
Patients requiring reversal of the effects of oral anticoagulants
Coagulation is measured using a conventional coagulation laboratory, a calibrated anti-Xa level, a ClotPro, a ROTEM and a GEM Haemochron. Measurements are taken before administration of andexanet alfa or PPSB, and 15 minutes, 2 hours

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Certain or probable intake of a factor Xa antagonist within the last 24 hours
- Referral to the 24/7 anticoagulation service by the doctor on duty, in accordance with internal SOPs
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with known hereditary coagulation disorders (von Willebrand syndrome, haemophilia A, B or C, factor VII deficiency, hereditary thrombocytopathies)
